messages:
Jordan (PM): quick sync: prototype link for scorecard filter persistence + tiny accessibility nits. want to decide before we freeze copy for launch. https://www.figma.com/proto/abcd/scorecards Anya (Design): main ask: should filters persist across sessions or reset per-run? UX opinion: persist last used per-user per-project. avoids repeated setup for repeated work. Priya (Accessibility): persisting is fine if we expose a clear label and allow a way to reset. keyboard users should be able to clear filters with a single control (e.g., 'Clear filters' button). ensure the button is reachable and has aria-label. Mike (Eng): persisting on server-side per-user adds infra work (small). alternative: client-side localStorage with an opt-in toggle in settings. which do we want? Lena (Product): preference for server-side so shortcuts and consistency across devices. but fallback to client-side if user is offline. we should scope to project. Sam (DevEx): doc note: we need an API flag for "persisted_filters=true/false" and telemetry when filters reset. also add a keyboard shortcut to focus filter bar ("/"). Anya (Design): microcopy idea: when filters are active show a tiny pill: "Filters saved" with tooltip "Saved to your workspace settings" and a clear (x). avoids modal. Priya (Accessibility): a11y: pill must have aria-live updates when filters auto-apply on load (announce what filters applied). Example:
Applied filters: Reviewer=Anya, Status=Pending
Ciara (DesignOps): small ops question: should clearing filters be auditable? security teams may ask if approvals or mass changes were made under certain filter contexts. Jordan (PM): good point. audit log should record actions, not filter state, but we can include filter snapshot in the event metadata for bulk approvals only. Sam can we capture that? Sam (DevEx): yes we can attach a hashed filter snapshot to bulk action events. store as short string, not full PII. Mike (Eng): accessibility table header nit: in compact mode we removed explicit for visual simplicity. Priya flagged that screen readers lose table semantics. we should restore but visually hide with .sr-only if needed. Priya (Accessibility): exactly. use CSS like .sr-only or aria-labels. also ensure each row has aria-describedby linking to summary badge for differences. Anya (Design): layout question: comment counts currently show on hover. mobile has no hover so we show inline. does that feel cluttered? Lena (Product): inline counts on mobile okay. perhaps show a condensed icon with number and reveal full text on tap. keep desktop hover detail. Jordan (PM): mobile gesture idea: swipe right to mark reviewed, swipe left for quick actions. discoverability concerns. Mike (Eng): implementable but needs careful touch handling. gestures conflict with native scroll. must provide keyboard equivalents. Priya (Accessibility): gestures not accessible by keyboard/screenreader. ensure alternate buttons for all gesture actions and ARIA hints. Anya (Design): maybe gesture is optional behind a setting. default off. Ciara (DesignOps): rollout suggestion: feature flag for 10% mobile users, gather metrics: success rate, accidental activations, keyboard coverage. Jordan (PM): prioritize: A) restore table semantics + aria fixes, B) server-side filter persistence + pill UI, C) audit metadata for bulk actions, D) mobile gestures behind flag. Sam (DevEx): I'll add telemetry specs, API flag, and keyboard shortcuts docs. Mike (Eng): I'll start a small PR for table semantics and add e2e accessibility checks. Priya (Accessibility): I'll review PR and provide exact aria snippets. e.g. Diff Anya (Design): I'll update Figma with pill states and mobile quick-actions mock. Lena (Product): Thanks. Jordan will update the ticket with priorities and assign owners. audit-bot: Logged decision: "persist filters server-side (project scoped)". Jordan (PM): copy nit: change "Save filters" to "Save filters to workspace" for clarity. schedule accessibility review for next Thursday.
